humanReview.verdict: rejected — agent self-scores were inflated; every category re-scored from the board against the turnaround

frontProfileSilhouette.label: front/profile silhouette
frontProfileSilhouette.note: Critic (round 3 final): Blocker (a) IS cleared: I re-extracted the shoulder from junebug-profile-review.png onto a green backdrop at 2.6x gain (F2-shoulder-boost) and no background shows through the cuff — the dark open interior is gone, the arm fills the ring. Blocker (b) is HALF cleared. Forearm mass measured on junebug-front-review.png: vertical thickness at mid-forearm (x=120..140) is 27-29 px against a 166 px head width = 0.169 head-widths; the turnaround's hanging forearm (y600-615) is 34 px against a 250 px head width = 0.136. The forearm is now if anything chunkier than the concept. The HAND is not: junebug-front-review.png shows four flat, uniformly-thin, sharply-pointed finger slabs splayed like a rake plus a stub thumb, where junebug-turnaround.png draws a rounded grouped mitten paddle. 3.1's five also asks for organic transitions everywhere and three junctions are still butt joints visible on the board: the sleeve meets the torso on a hard straight diagonal cut with two detached white stripe shards floating beside the cuff (junebug-profile-review.png shoulder), the pelvis is a flat overhanging shelf with thigh cylinders joined under it (junebug-front-review.png waist/legs), and the shoe sole is a flat cardboard plate (junebug-front-review.png). Partly addressed = 4.

headBodyProportions.label: head/body proportions
headBodyProportions.note: Critic (round 3 final): MEASURED per 3.13, not eyeballed. Definitions applied identically to both images; head top = first row wider than half max head width scanning down (excludes bun), chin = last row wider than 1.5x neck width. TURNAROUND front figure: head 250 w x 244 h px, ratio 1.025. junebug-front-review.png: head 166 w x 156 h px, ratio 1.064. Second measure, face skin span at the eye line : hairline-to-chin — turnaround 249:163 = 1.53, render 164:101 = 1.62. Forehead (hairline bottom to brow top, sampled at both brow columns) — turnaround 50.5 px = 0.207 of head height, render 30 px = 0.192. Width carried to the jaw (width at 75% down / max width) — turnaround 0.96, render 0.97. Head:standing height — turnaround 244/878 = 0.278, render 156/578 = 0.270. On every one of those the skull is now within 4-6% of the concept and no longer long or narrow, so two of the three do-items are genuinely done. The third is not: temples. Skin width at the brow row / head width is 226/250 = 0.90 on the turnaround but only 130/166 = 0.78 on junebug-front-review.png, because the hair wedge occupies 13.9% of head width at that row against the concept's 2.8%. The bone is unpinched; the face still reads pinched. 3.2 also wants joints reading as connected forms and the hip is a butt-joined shelf. Partly addressed = 4.

hairMass.label: hair mass
hairMass.note: Critic (round 3 final): The painted corduroy is gone — the crown in H-render-crown (from junebug-front-review.png) is clean, no highlight banding. But the replacement is a completely featureless smooth dome with ZERO sculpted strand grooves, front or profile (junebug-profile-review.png crown is one unbroken brown blob). Rubric 3.3 caps that at 4 in its own words: 'a smooth featureless blob caps at 4 however correct its silhouette'. The bun is still a two-lobe stack with a hard horizontal ledge where the shelves meet (junebug-profile-review.png, and the same step in junebug-front-review.png). The temple taper is not fixed: junebug-front-review.png shows the hair coming down each side of the face as a broad mass with a straight hard diagonal edge terminating in a sharp point at cheek level and overlapping the ear, measured at 13.9% of head width at the brow row against the turnaround's 2.8% — 5x too heavy. junebug-runtime-run.png shows the same hard wedge edge cutting across the cheek. Silhouette (designed mass, hairline reads front and side, no bare skull) holds, so 4, but it is the weakest 4 of the six.

clothingConstruction.label: clothing construction
clothingConstruction.note: Critic (round 3 final): The named blocker is mostly gone. junebug-front-review.png waist now reads jersey hem -> belt -> pants, not three stacked garments, and the belt carries two salmon loops and a central dark buckle block. Two things keep it off 5. First, the belt is inset: in silhouette it is narrower than both the jersey above and the pants below, so both sides show a corset step and the belt reads as a cinched ring rather than a strap lying on the pants — the turnaround's belt is flush with the waist. Second, 3.4's bar is 'cuffs, hems, soles, laces' and the shoes fail it outright in junebug-front-review.png: no laces, no eyelets, no tongue, no heel counter, a flat overhanging plate for a sole, and a single painted grey rectangle standing in for the lacing. The shoe's colour is also inverted against the contract — the render is a red shoe with a white toe oval, the turnaround is a white shoe with a red toe cap and red stripes. The jersey hem is a hard squared box edge with visible corner notches rather than a draping hem. Partly addressed = 4.

faceExpressionRead.label: face/expression read
faceExpressionRead.note: Critic (round 3 final): None of the three named blockers is gone. (a) Ears fail binary 3.10 outright. junebug-front-review.png shows a flat, faceted, skin-coloured wedge with a hard straight edge at each side — no outer rim, no inner shadow hollow, no lobe; the turnaround's ear at the same zoom has all three plus a curled helix. junebug-profile-review.png improves it to a rounded pad with a faint edge but still no concha shadow and no lobe, and it is placed too low: the render's widest head row sits at 71% of head height (eye centre 69%), while the turnaround's silhouette steps outward for the ears starting at 60%, above the eye. That step is itself measurable — the concept gains 13.6% of head width in 16 rows (6.6% of head height); the render gains only 8.4% gradually over 20 rows, i.e. there is no ear in the front silhouette at all. (b) The nose still does not catch light head-on. Measured on junebug-front-review.png: nose bridge/tip mean luminance 116.7 against lit cheek 116.5 — zero separation; it only reads because the opposite cheek is in shadow at 90.7. On junebug-turnaround.png the nose is 123.1 against cheeks of 115.6 and 112.7, i.e. +8 to +10 above BOTH. (c) The face is still a sticker. junebug-runtime-hero.png and junebug-runtime-run.png both show a rectangular tonal panel around the eye, a hard vertical seam dropping from the outer brow, and hard polygon facets crossing the cheek and jaw, so the features are not integrated with the skull's planes. Mouth is a small dark slot with no lip form at hero scale (3.14 pressure). Zero of three blockers cleared = 3.

heroAndFieldScale.label: hero + 40px read
heroAndFieldScale.note: Critic (round 3 final): Blocker not cleared. I did a true downscale of junebug-front-review.png to a 16x40 sprite and viewed it nearest-upscaled beside the same treatment of the turnaround. The bun does read as a lump, so that half works. The headband does not: measured mean rgb(199,198,195) — a neutral mid grey — against the turnaround's rgb(250,242,234) warm white, 45 luminance points darker, with peak 210 against the concept's 255. Headband-vs-hair Michelson contrast is 0.521 on the render against 0.635 on the concept, 18% lower, and at 40 px the grey band and the brown bun merge into a single grey-brown cap where the concept still shows a bright white stripe under a dark bun. The brief's instruction was explicitly 'bright white with maximum contrast against both hair and skin'; it is measurably not met. Sleeve stripes are grey not bright (cuff sample peak 190) and disappear at 40 px. At hero scale junebug-runtime-hero.png adds two identity breaks against the turnaround: the ponytail tie renders yellow/gold, measured mean rgb(83,74,36), hue 48 degrees, where the concept's tie is neutral white — and the same yellow is present in junebug-runtime-run.png, so it is not a one-frame artefact — and the ponytail tip is a flat navy-grey wedge instead of the concept's brown hooked arrow. If the tie is the declared team-accent surface that needs saying in the receipt, because as filed the hero evidence does not match the contract. Face collapse at 40 px is improved but the band contrast and the tie colour keep this at 3.
